items.title: Exact big Ramsey degree four for two-element subsets of the ordered set of integers
items.author: Joanna Boyland; William Gasarch; Nathan Hurtig; Robert Rust
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement fixes the big Ramsey degree of the ordered set of integers for pairs, T(2,zeta) = 4, so both a four-colour upper bound for an arbitrary finite colouring and a four-colouring that no order-equivalent copy can reduce have to be produced, and the two directions use different constructions. The upper bound at source lines 499-513 replaces the colouring of the pairs of zeta by the four-tuple colouring of the pairs of omega that records the four sign combinations, and then rebuilds a copy of zeta from the homogeneous set G by alternating signs with the parity of the index, H = {-h_i : i even} + {h_i : i odd}; the author's aside at source line 511 states that exactly this alternation is what guarantees that the two absolute values are distinct, a condition the four-tuple bookkeeping does not control by itself. The lower bound at source lines 515-537 needs a case analysis that a routine appeal to Ramsey's theorem does not supply: the four-colouring is defined by the signs of the two entries and by the comparison of their absolute values, and for an arbitrary H that is order-equivalent to zeta one must first see that H contains a pair in each of the four cases before all four colours can be claimed. Applying Ramsey's theorem directly to zeta is not available here, because the theorem is stated for the naturals and the reconstruction of a zeta-copy is the actual work.
